question: What's the status of Atlas?

invariants.$comment_allowed_widening: Observed: scope_resolution_outcome='organization_fallback', allowed=['ambiguous'] (receipt tests/acceptance/artifacts/wave4/scope.ambiguous.json). The ambiguity IS detected and IS still asserted by this case: resolution_path_in PASSED in the same receipt with resolution_path='miss-clarification', which derive_resolution_path only returns when a mention never converged on a committed subject. What the run does NOT do is put AMBIGUOUS on the wire -- scope_service.py:730/:1146 are the only producers of that value and the preflight miss path does not reach them; it widens through subject_preflight.py:863 instead. So the case keeps its ambiguity proof and stops asserting a wire value the ambiguity path never emits. CHAOS-3490 Part 2 / CHAOS-3219 Phase 2 exit, run 7 (world digest 2e1e254d3ee8b799fd58234e865ccf1361c2753c412d1b526bf4e79d1e445232, wave_3_1 preflight enabled=True -- the first runs to measure the real CHAOS-3292 preflight path). The allowed list is WIDENED, not the expectation weakened: the profile keeps its honest primary expected_scope_resolution_outcome and this invariant additionally accepts organization_fallback, which is the DISCLOSED widening this invariant's own 'assert' prose already names as acceptable (\"widening is only ever a disclosed, terminal answered_with_gaps/needs_clarification outcome\"). Disclosure proved live, not assumed -- .p2exit-logs/probe-widening-acr.log and probe-widening-wordorder.log, run 61ba05f7-2d14-4d56-8cc3-b811000d9fa1, scope.resolved frame: outcome='organization_fallback', fallbacks=['organization'], resolved_scope.direct_scope='organization', answer terminal answered_with_gaps with subject_ref null and a direct_summary that never claims to have answered about the named subject. Production reaches it through subject_preflight.py:863 _organization_wide_result, whose DevScopeResolution is required by contracts.py:416-423 to carry organization scope -- a machine consumer reading dev_scope_resolution.v1 can see exactly what happened. A silent widen (org scope with outcome='exact' and no fallbacks) is still caught, because that is a different enum value and is not in this list.
invariants.assert: A named subject mention that misses its intended target never silently widens to org-wide/broader scope; widening is only ever a disclosed, terminal answered_with_gaps/needs_clarification outcome.
invariants.$comment: Wired to the real graduated checker scope_resolution_outcome_in against this case's own resolution-profile expected_scope_resolution_outcome (rebase pass, 2a landed the 3 graduated checkers in PR #1518) -- no longer a narrower no_internal_error placeholder.

invariants.assert: A run that widens scope must reach a DISCLOSED terminal -- the widening is never absorbed into a terminal that reads as an ordinary, subject-specific answer.
invariants.$comment: CHAOS-3490 Part 2, closing an adversarial-review finding (2026-08-07). scope_resolution_outcome_in checks only the outcome ENUM; this case's no-silent-widening assert prose additionally requires the widening to be DISCLOSED, and nothing asserted that half. The gap was real and narrow: before the allowed list was widened, ANY organization_fallback failed by accident (wrong enum); after widening, a run that genuinely widens but fails the disclosure half would have passed. Nothing structural closes it -- validate_outcome_consistency only checks frame self-consistency, and the CHAOS-3421 leak guard is a text heuristic. Wired via from_profile so the profile stays the single source of truth rather than a literal pair chosen here.

invariants.assert: Every candidate offered (ranked or unranked) is drawn from the requester's own authorized catalog (permission_fingerprint-scoped); a candidate outside that scope must never appear.
invariants.$comment: Wired to the real graduated checker no_unauthorized_candidate_surfaces with a literal authorized_entity_ids allowlist -- org primary's full real fixture repository/project/team catalog, derived directly from src/dev_health_ops/fixtures/generator.py's FIXTURE_NAMESPACE uuid5 repo-id derivation, fixtures/generators/projects.py (project id = repo_full_name), and fixtures/demo_identity.py + world.py's postprocess (team id = literal slug); cross-checked against subjects.json + sources.json's org_alias=primary roster (rebase pass, 2a landed the 3 graduated checkers in PR #1518). Deliberately excludes subject.tenant.sibling-only-private-repo's sibling-org derived ids -- the whole point of this invariant is that they must never appear here. KNOWN TRUST BOUNDARY (invariants.py's own docstring): this declared list's correctness is case-authoring's responsibility, not independently re-verified by the checker at runtime.
